events.title: Gallery Walk at the Museum
events.description:
It’s the holiday season: Main Street is all lit up, the Festival of Miniatures is in full swing, Brattleboro’s fantastic retailers are ready to meet all your holiday shopping needs, and we’re staying open late!

Drop by between 5 and 8 p.m. to check out the six exhibitions on view and connect with new and old friends.

events.title: Art Talk: Amy Beecher on Glotech Cantata
events.description:
Amy Beecher discusses Glotech Cantata—a performance of movement, sound, and still images that interprets the dance between women and influencer marketing. Taking the Glotech LED facial mask as its motif, the work meditates upon our era of aspirational social media, where women are both the authors and the objects of images. This site-responsive performance uses “paintings”—large printed panels of still lifes, masks, and color abstractions—as both props and a movable set that frame, conceal, and cast color onto dancers, who pit improvised movements against stylized gestures and words.

Glotech Cantata was written, directed, and designed by Amy Beecher, with original choreography by Tess Dworman and sound design by Ryan Gamblin. It will be performed by Hilary Clark, Jessica Cook, and Mariana Valencia at the Campus at Marlboro Music on Sunday, December 13, at 12 p.m.

Thank You

This project is funded in part by a Faculty Advancement Grant and a Research Assistance Grant from Emerson College, Boston, MA, and a Foundation for Contemporary Arts Emergency Grant.

events.title: Model Railroads at Union Station
events.description:
In connection with the Brattleboro Festival of Miniatures, we’re filling our former train station building with a dazzling assortment of working model railroads and dioramas.

Drop by during regular open hours to see a Lionel 1939 Commodore Vanderbilt O-gauge streamliner, a 160-square-foot recreation of the Boston & Maine Northern Line from Concord, N.H. to White River Junction, Vt., and more.

events.title: Workshop: Creating Acorn Creatures
events.description:
Taking inspiration from David M. Bird’s wondrous Becorns, now on view at BMAC, this workshop for makers of all ages and experience levels will guide participants in creating their own special creatures out of natural materials. Bring your own twigs, leaves, seeds, and shells, or draw upon our extensive stash of supplies. Instructor Ross Smart will help get the creative juices flowing and will guide you in the use of materials, tools, and techniques.

Note: David M. Bird will not be present for this workshop.

events.title: A Feast for All Senses: Dinner Inspired by Hayal Pozanti
events.description:
Chef Erin Bevan brings her culinary imagination to BMAC, creating a four-course dinner inspired by the lush colors, organic forms, and dreamlike landscapes of Hayal Pozanti’s The World Sang Through Me. Served in the Wolf Kahn & Emily Mason Gallery, surrounded by Pozanti’s paintings, this feast for the senses invites guests to experience art in a new way—through flavor, texture, aroma, and the pleasures of a shared meal.

For Bevan, the connections between art, food, and nature run deep. Raised on a small farm in western Massachusetts, she grew up harvesting, foraging, and cooking with what the land provided. She later studied sculpture before discovering a new artistic medium in food. After years in acclaimed kitchens in Boston and southern Vermont, she now creates intimate, inventive dining experiences that celebrate the seasons and draw on her relationships with local farmers and producers.

To inquire about dietary restrictions, call 802-257-0124 x101 or email office@brattleboromuseum.org before purchasing tickets.

events.title: Symposium: Immigrant Artists in Vermont
events.description:
What has drawn immigrant artists to Vermont over the past two centuries? How has Vermont shaped their work, and how have these artists, in turn, shaped Vermont’s evolving cultural identity?

Through presentations, panel discussions, and audience Q&A, this symposium explores the experiences and contributions of immigrant artists in Vermont, from the stonecutters of Barre and Proctor and the founders of Marlboro Music to influential puppeteers and generations of landscape painters.

Four sessions on Saturday will be followed by an evening celebration featuring food and performances. A concluding panel on Sunday will bring together immigrant artists living and working in Vermont today to reflect on their experiences and look toward the future.

Additional details will be announced.

Image: Luigi Lucioni, Northern Lombardy (detail) (1938), oil on canvas, 14 x 24 inches. Collection of Shelburne Museum, bequest of Luigi Lucioni, 1988-27.3. Photography by Andy Duback.

Thank You

This event is supported by a grant from the Vilcek Foundation.

events.title: Art Talk: Sara Jimenez & Sarah Freeman
events.description:
Artist Sara Jimenez and curator Sarah Freeman discuss Jimenez’s installation the story never stops beginning or ending, exploring how textiles, ceramics, and collaged imagery bring together personal memory and histories of American colonization in the Philippines. Through layered landscapes and sculptural forms honoring Filipino women and non-binary individuals, Jimenez creates a space for reflection on history, remembrance, and care.

Sara Jimenez’s work gives form to histories that are often unseen or forgotten, exploring the shifting connections between ancestors, land, memory, and the present. Working across installation, sculpture, collage, and performance, she creates fantastical environments and otherworldly, biomorphic objects that transform these histories into visual metaphors.

Drawing from her kaleidoscopic connection to her genealogical roots in the Philippines, Southeast Asia, the Pacific, and the ancient United Kingdom, Jimenez considers how histories change as they move between places and generations, and how forms of memory can exist outside official records.

She draws on archival sources, historical narratives, family histories, and material culture, while also attending to the gaps and silences within official histories. She is interested in forms of resistance and survival that are often overlooked, including the preservation of knowledge, movement through landscapes, and the transmission of cultural memory.

Jimenez uses color, abstraction, and fantastical forms to complicate conventional ideas of monuments and memorials. Rather than presenting history as fixed or complete, her installations consider how objects can transform meaning and unearth history, while her sculptures create alternative ways of remembering. Her site-responsive projects extend this inquiry by responding to the particular histories, architectures, and landscapes of the places where they are made.

Sara Jimenez received her BA from the University of Toronto and her MFA from Parsons School of Design at The New School. Selected solo exhibitions include Rachel Uffner Gallery, Smack Mellon, and Morgan Lehman Gallery, all in New York City. Selected commissions include Cornell University in Ithaca, New York; Wave Hill in New York; and MadArt Studio in Seattle. Jimenez has also exhibited at El Museo del Barrio, The Brooklyn Museum, and The Bronx Museum. Her work is part of the permanent collection of the Ford Foundation Center for Social Justice. Selected awards and grants include the Canadian Women’s Artist Award from the New York Foundation for the Arts, multiple grants from the Canada Council for the Arts, and the Colene Brown Art Prize from BRIC (Brooklyn Information & Culture). Jimenez is represented by Chozick Family Art Gallery in New York City.

events.title: Nowruz: Where Hope Blossoms
events.description:
Join us for a joyful celebration of Nowruz, the Persian New Year, welcoming spring and new beginnings. Free and open to all, this event will bring people together through traditional music, art, and Afghan cultural traditions.
